result:
VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed solution gives no derivation. It cites a "known classification" and asserts that girth 5 occurs, but it never exhibits a group with girth 5. I could not verify that claim.

The girth 3 case is genuine. For $G=\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$, the three subgroups of order 2 pairwise multiply to $G$, so $\Gamma^*(G)$ is a triangle.

For the claim that girth 5 occurs, I did not find an example. The groups I checked either gave triangles or no cycle at all: $S_3$ and $A_4$ give stars, and $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_p^3$ contain triangles among the order-$p^2$ subgroups. My recollection of the literature on deleted co-maximal subgroup graphs is that the girth is 3 or 4 whenever a cycle exists, which would give $S=\{3,4\}$ and a sum of 7. I did not check the girth 4 construction in detail, so this is a recollection, not a verified result.

CONFIDENCE: 3
